## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment

  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via

- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:

- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

Important context: gh-1073 established that unbounded snapshot ledgers grew a session file to 12.4 GiB, and led to:
1. `ledgerTextCapChars` — every string field in a persisted ledger payload goes through a cap.
2. `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` — suppress repeated identical snapshots at the write site.

The obligations ledger BREAKS BOTH conventions deliberately:
- Entry `text` is UNBOUNDED verbatim (the whole user message — could be a 50KB pasted log that happens to contain "always" or "please"!). The PR says "Unlike those registries the entries are never paraphrases or caps — the text is the exact source span (AC2); the budget lives at render time only." So a user message of arbitrary size that matches a rule pattern is quoted VERBATIM into EVERY subsequent snapshot (each new classification appends a FULL snapshot — with all entries). Session file growth: every classified message appends a full copy of the ledger (all entries, unbounded texts). With long user prompts (this repo's users paste huge prompts), the file grows quadratically-ish in ledger content. gh-1073's 12.4 GiB lesson applies directly: the obligations ledger has NO deduper and NO caps.

Mitigations in this PR: population fires once per real user message (low frequency) — but "low frequency" was ALSO true of shell_job_registry mutations at first, and gh-1073 happened anyway. The PR explicitly defers the deduper to the per-turn classifier tier. The verbatim cap is a design conflict with AC2 (verbatim vs cap) — acknowledged.

The real quantifiable risk: a snapshot payload = sum of all entry texts. If a user session has N classified messages of average length L, the LAST snapshot is N*L chars, and the file carries ~N snapshots → O(N²L) bytes. With N=500 classified messages of L=2KB → 500 snapshots * 1MB avg = 500MB. That's exactly the gh-1073 blowup shape, minus the per-mutation frequency. It deserves an IMPORTANT (maybe BLOCKING?). The PR acknowledges "No snapshot deduper (gh-1073) — population fires once per real user message (low frequency)". It's disclosed as a deliberate ceiling. But gh-1073 is PRECEDENT: "low frequency" assumptions already caused a 12.4GiB file. The mitigation cost is low (wire the existing LedgerSnapshotDeduper at the write site — the deduper is already imported in agent_cli.dart). Hmm. The deduper only suppresses IDENTICAL consecutive snapshots — repeated identical snapshots don't happen here (each ingest changes the payload). The deduper wouldn't help! The actual growth driver is full-snapshot-per-mutation, which is the established pattern. So the only real lever is capping entry text — which AC2 forbids (verbatim). OR spilling: not storing text, storing record pointers + rendering reads from the source record — that's a redesign.

Actually wait — is there a cap I'm missing? `ObligationEntry.text` = full message text. `renderObligationsBlock` renders full text per line, but open entries ALWAYS render even over budget. So the CONTEXT cost is also unbounded: 500 open obligations → the block is megabytes of context, no matter the 6000-char budget! The "budget" only evicts CLOSED entries; open entries render in full. So a chatty user who says "please" in 200 messages permanently appends ~200 lines to every subsequent model context — 200 * message length. The E1 rule says "an obligation is never dropped by the budget" — by design. But there's NO lifecycle tool yet (mark_done tool is a LATER slice!). In this slice, entries can NEVER be closed (no tool, no auto-supersede, no contradiction detection — "ledger diff on resume; contradiction detection | second tier"). So in the shipped state, every matched message opens a PERMANENT open entry that renders forever at level 0, unbounded count, unbounded length, with no way to close it.

That's a real product-level hazard shipped by this slice: rule `/\b(please|can you|...)\b/` matches common phrasing ("please" appears in tons of messages); each match permanently injects the FULL message text into every future model context. A user who says "please" in 100 messages gets 100 verbatim message quotes appended to every turn. Context bloat + file growth + noise that drowns the actual obligations. The 6000-char budget does NOTHING for open entries (they always render).

Hmm, but precision-first: the classifier matches "can you", "please" — extremely common. The PR's own test shows "can you also fix the flake, please" → open-ask. Real-world user messages: "can you check" → permanent open-ask. There's no dedup of similar texts either ("could you look into X" then "could you look into X tomorrow" → 2 entries). This is the known v1 scope (rule-based v1, precision over recall — though "please/can you" is NOT precise...). The epic later adds mark_done + smol classifier tier. The budget follow-up adds "open-spill into checkpoint text".

Should this be BLOCKING? It's not a "bug" per se — it's the designed v1 behavior with a documented follow-up. But the combination (no way to close entries in this slice + open-always-renders + loose regex) means the shipped slice can materially degrade context quality in long real sessions. The PR discloses the budget ceilings but NOT the "no way to close entries in v1" consequence — actually it does implicitly (mark_done is a listed later slice; ObligationsLedgerWriter.markStatus "already lands as its substrate"). Reviewer judgment: IMPORTANT, not BLOCKING — it works as designed, matches the epic's plan, and the severity rule says BLOCKING = broken behavior/bug/data-loss. This is a design risk. I'll make it IMPORTANT with concrete numbers.

Back to file growth: snapshots append per classification, each carrying all entries verbatim. With no deduper (won't help anyway), the gh-1073 lesson is partially mitigated by "once per real user message" frequency. I'll fold file growth into the same IMPORTANT finding (context + file growth from unbounded open set).

- Default CLI resume path is windowed (`windowed: true` at session_commands.dart:572) for marathon sessions (exactly the sessions with obligations).
- Once the latest ledger snapshot is below the resident tail, the block silently vanishes (AC1 broken in the shipped host) AND the next classification persists a wholesale snapshot that permanently erases prior entries (data loss of the feature's own state).
- Precedent: issue #488 — the sibling registry came back EMPTY on EVERY windowed restart; fixed by raw-file scan. - The HARD invariant of the epic ("compaction can never sink an obligation") is violated by the shipped host in the very scenario the invariant exists for.

Arguments for IMPORTANT: it's disclosed as a deliberate ceiling tied to a known issue class; the owner may accept it for slice 1.

The verdict rules: "BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates, scope violations, security issues, data loss." Silent permanent erasure of ledger state = data loss, and the block vanishing = broken behavior of the slice's one HARD invariant, on the default path of the shipped host. The disclosure frames it as a projection-only miss ("missed snapshot") and misses the wholesale-erase amplification. I'll mark it BLOCKING. That means recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking: 1.

Hmm, let me double-check the wholesale-erase claim once more. `latestObligationsLedgerIn(await session.getEntries())` on a windowed storage returns the latest RESIDENT snapshot. If ANY ledger snapshot is resident (e.g. recent ones), the writer starts from it — entries older than the window are already gone from that snapshot? NO — snapshots are cumulative: the latest snapshot contains ALL entries ever (each snapshot is the full ledger). So if the LATEST snapshot is resident, the writer has the full state. The erase scenario requires the LATEST snapshot itself to be non-resident (below the compaction boundary), while a message later gets classified → writer starts from older-resident-snapshot or empty → persists snapshot missing the newer entries → but those newer entries' snapshots are non-resident anyway... wait, if the latest snapshot is non-resident, the resident tail starts AFTER it. The file-level latest snapshot then becomes the new one — the pre-boundary entries are ERASED from the effective ledger (file still has the old snapshots as audit, but latest-wins). So yes: whenever the latest ledger snapshot falls below the windowed tail and a new classification fires, every entry after that older snapshot is permanently dropped from the effective ledger. And the projection meanwhile shows a stale-or-empty block.

How likely is the latest snapshot to be non-resident at classification time? Timeline: snapshot appended at message persist → the record is at the leaf → resident. It stays resident until the window slides past it (residency cap ~ records) OR a resume pages back only to the newest compaction boundary (records below boundary non-resident). Compaction boundary = newest classic CompactionRecord... and the token budget cap. So: marathon resume with parity budget → tail covers ~1 window of tokens → a ledger snapshot older than that window of tokens is non-resident. If the user then says "always do X" → writer rehydrates from whatever ledger snapshots ARE resident (possibly none) → snapshot persisted missing all earlier entries. Real and reachable. Also the mid-session auto-compaction on windowed storage prunes via _dropOldest by residency cap — same effect live.

OK — BLOCKING it is. It also has a trivial mitigation available in this slice: reuse the raw-scan (`subagentRegistryRows` pattern) OR gate `_ingestObligations` rehydration on full residency. I'll note the fix.

Second candidate BLOCKING: none. The engine-gate mismatch (liveCompactionEngine) — IMPORTANT.

**Why this slice first.** The GOAL names three additions (A1 ledger, A2 `session_search`, A3 prompt contract) without ranking them. This lane took the **A1 data model + projection** — the smallest self-contained slice with real consumer value, and the one carrying the epic's only HARD invariant (compaction can never sink an obligation below the visible surface — the generalization of #148's S2). A2's search and A3's prompt block both *consume* the ledger's record kind and vocabulary; landing the substrate first gives every later slice its foundation. Population follows the body's Q1 proposal: **rule-based v1** (deterministic, precision-first — a misclassifying judge must never invent obligations), smol-role classifier stays second tier.

### What's in

- **`lib/src/session/obligations_ledger.dart` (new)** — the substrate:
  - `ObligationEntry` `{kind: owner-rule|open-ask|agent-commitment|pending-wait, text: VERBATIM, sourceRecordId, createdAt, status: open|done|superseded}`; lifecycle transitions keep the entry (auditable "you said X then Y", E2).
  - Tolerant parse (E6): missing fields default, unknown kind/status stay visible, junk payload never throws — forward-compatible with older/newer writers.
  - `renderObligationsBlock`: compact `<system-notice>` block; **open entries always render** (an obligation is never dropped by the budget); over budget the oldest *closed* entries evict first (E1). Default budget 6k chars ≈ the body's ≤1%-of-window proposal; window-coupled wiring is a follow-up.
  - Rule-based classifier + `ObligationsLedgerWriter` (idempotent per source record — a record never opens twice).
- **Record kind**: `obligations_ledger` `custom` record, latest-snapshot-wins (the established `shell_job_registry`/`subagent_registry` pattern — no parallel second system, no parse-switch change, byte-preserving JSONL). Joins `repairKeepLatestCustomTypes` (repair-safe) and the trajectory `hiddenCustomRecordTypes` (no unknown-record rows).
- **Level-0 projection (the hard invariant)**: `Session._projectMessages` appends the rendered block **after every projected message** — outside any hidden range or checkpoint span by construction, so hide/compact/flatten at any depth cannot sink it. Presence-gated on the latest snapshot record: a session without one projects **byte-identically** (E3, classic engine included). Snapshot reads go through `getEntries()` (file order), so even a classic cut that drops the snapshot record itself from the kept region cannot sink the block.
- **Population wiring (CLI host)**: each persisted real-user message is classified under the structure

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name

- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

Important context: gh-1073 established that unbounded snapshot ledgers grew a session file to 12.4 GiB, and led to:
1. `ledgerTextCapChars` — every string field in a persisted ledger payload goes through a cap.
2. `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` — suppress repeated identical snapshots at the write site.

The obligations ledger BREAKS BOTH conventions deliberately:
- Entry `text` is UNBOUNDED verbatim (the whole user message — could be a 50KB pasted log that happens to contain "always" or "please"!). The PR says "Unlike those registries the entries are never paraphrases or caps — the text is the exact source span (AC2); the budget lives at render time only." So a user message of arbitrary size that matches a rule pattern is quoted VERBATIM into EVERY subsequent snapshot (each new classification appends a FULL snapshot — with all entries). Session file growth: every classified message appends a full copy of the ledger (all entries, unbounded texts). With long user prompts (this repo's users paste huge prompts), the file grows quadratically-ish in ledger content. gh-1073's 12.4 GiB lesson applies directly: the obligations ledger has NO deduper and NO caps.

Mitigations in this PR: population fires once per real user message (low frequency) — but "low frequency" was ALSO true of shell_job_registry mutations at first, and gh-1073 happened anyway. The PR explicitly defers the deduper to the per-turn classifier tier. The verbatim cap is a design conflict with AC2 (verbatim vs cap) — acknowledged.

The real quantifiable risk: a snapshot payload = sum of all entry texts. If a user session has N classified messages of average length L, the LAST snapshot is N*L chars, and the file carries ~N snapshots → O(N²L) bytes. With N=500 classified messages of L=2KB → 500 snapshots * 1MB avg = 500MB. That's exactly the gh-1073 blowup shape, minus the per-mutation frequency. It deserves an IMPORTANT (maybe BLOCKING?). The PR acknowledges "No snapshot deduper (gh-1073) — population fires once per real user message (low frequency)". It's disclosed as a deliberate ceiling. But gh-1073 is PRECEDENT: "low frequency" assumptions already caused a 12.4GiB file. The mitigation cost is low (wire the existing LedgerSnapshotDeduper at the write site — the deduper is already imported in agent_cli.dart). Hmm. The deduper only suppresses IDENTICAL consecutive snapshots — repeated identical snapshots don't happen here (each ingest changes the payload). The deduper wouldn't help! The actual growth driver is full-snapshot-per-mutation, which is the established pattern. So the only real lever is capping entry text — which AC2 forbids (verbatim). OR spilling: not storing text, storing record pointers + rendering reads from the source record — that's a redesign.

Actually wait — is there a cap I'm missing? `ObligationEntry.text` = full message text. `renderObligationsBlock` renders full text per line, but open entries ALWAYS render even over budget. So the CONTEXT cost is also unbounded: 500 open obligations → the block is megabytes of context, no matter the 6000-char budget! The "budget" only evicts CLOSED entries; open entries render in full. So a chatty user who says "please" in 200 messages permanently appends ~200 lines to every subsequent model context — 200 * message length. The E1 rule says "an obligation is never dropped by the budget" — by design. But there's NO lifecycle tool yet (mark_done tool is a LATER slice!). In this slice, entries can NEVER be closed (no tool, no auto-supersede, no contradiction detection — "ledger diff on resume; contradiction detection | second tier"). So in the shipped state, every matched message opens a PERMANENT open entry that renders forever at level 0, unbounded count, unbounded length, with no way to close it.

That's a real product-level hazard shipped by this slice: rule `/\b(please|can you|...)\b/` matches common phrasing ("please" appears in tons of messages); each match permanently injects the FULL message text into every future model context. A user who says "please" in 100 messages gets 100 verbatim message quotes appended to every turn. Context bloat + file growth + noise that drowns the actual obligations. The 6000-char budget does NOTHING for open entries (they always render).

Hmm, but precision-first: the classifier matches "can you", "please" — extremely common. The PR's own test shows "can you also fix the flake, please" → open-ask. Real-world user messages: "can you check" → permanent open-ask. There's no dedup of similar texts either ("could you look into X" then "could you look into X tomorrow" → 2 entries). This is the known v1 scope (rule-based v1, precision over recall — though "please/can you" is NOT precise...). The epic later adds mark_done + smol classifier tier. The budget follow-up adds "open-spill into checkpoint text".

Should this be BLOCKING? It's not a "bug" per se — it's the designed v1 behavior with a documented follow-up. But the combination (no way to close entries in this slice + open-always-renders + loose regex) means the shipped slice can materially degrade context quality in long real sessions. The PR discloses the budget ceilings but NOT the "no way to close entries in v1" consequence — actually it does implicitly (mark_done is a listed later slice; ObligationsLedgerWriter.markStatus "already lands as its substrate"). Reviewer judgment: IMPORTANT, not BLOCKING — it works as designed, matches the epic's plan, and the severity rule says BLOCKING = broken behavior/bug/data-loss. This is a design risk. I'll make it IMPORTANT with concrete numbers.

Back to file growth: snapshots append per classification, each carrying all entries verbatim. With no deduper (won't help anyway), the gh-1073 lesson is partially mitigated by "once per real user message" frequency. I'll fold file growth into the same IMPORTANT finding (context + file growth from unbounded open set).

- Default CLI resume path is windowed (`windowed: true` at session_commands.dart:572) for marathon sessions (exactly the sessions with obligations).
- Once the latest ledger snapshot is below the resident tail, the block silently vanishes (AC1 broken in the shipped host) AND the next classification persists a wholesale snapshot that permanently erases prior entries (data loss of the feature's own state).
- Precedent: issue #488 — the sibling registry came back EMPTY on EVERY windowed restart; fixed by raw-file scan. - The HARD invariant of the epic ("compaction can never sink an obligation") is violated by the shipped host in the very scenario the invariant exists for.

Arguments for IMPORTANT: it's disclosed as a deliberate ceiling tied to a known issue class; the owner may accept it for slice 1.

The verdict rules: "BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates, scope violations, security issues, data loss." Silent permanent erasure of ledger state = data loss, and the block vanishing = broken behavior of the slice's one HARD invariant, on the default path of the shipped host. The disclosure frames it as a projection-only miss ("missed snapshot") and misses the wholesale-erase amplification. I'll mark it BLOCKING. That means recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking: 1.

NO — snapshots are cumulative: the latest snapshot contains ALL entries ever (each snapshot is the full ledger). So if the LATEST snapshot is resident, the writer has the full state. Very interesting. The comment at agent_cli.dart:454-457 documents that "the windowed boot open drops side-leaf custom records out of getEntries — the registry used to come back EMPTY on every restart" — issue #488 AC2 required a RAW FILE SCAN (`subagentRegistryRows`) for exactly this reason. The obligations ledger deliberately does NOT do the raw scan (documented ceiling). But the precedent (#488) shows this is NOT hypothetical — the subagent registry came back EMPTY on every restart until the raw scan was added. So the obligations ledger rehydration has a KNOWN, PRECEDENTED failure mode: on a windowed marathon resume, the latest ledger snapshot may be out of residency → `latestObligationsLedgerIn` returns null → projection renders NO block even though the session has open obligations. AND WORSE: the writer rehydrates from `getEntries()` too — so on resume, `_obligationsWriterFor` builds a writer from an EMPTY/stale ledger, and the next classification persists a snapshot that WHOLESALE REPLACES the true ledger (latest-snapshot-wins) — silently DROPPING all previously-open obligations from the ledger permanently, not just from one projection!

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent

`isSyntheticUserText`:
- `<system-notice>` anywhere (hasMatch)
- `^The following is a summary of a branch`
- `^from\s+\S+:\s` (mail)

`_syntheticUserPattern` (obligations_ledger.dart):
- `^\[(widget|ext:)` (extra — attach-view forms?)
- `^<system-notice>` prefix only
- `^<system-interrupt` (extra)
- `^from \S+: ` single space literal
- `^The following is a summary of a branch`

Drift consequences: a user message like "please <system-notice>..." — actually a real user typing "<system-notice>" mid-text would be classified by isSyntheticUserText (skipped) but the obligations classifier would treat prefix-only → would classify. Conversely agent mail with tabs "from\tagent-x:\t..." — isSynthetic matches (`\s+`), obligations doesn't (`from ` literal space) → mail could open an obligation ("from agent-x: could you also ..."). Multi-space/tab mail: `from  agent-x: ...` — `^from \S+: ` requires exactly one space after "from". `from\s+\S+:\s` in compaction allows multiple. So tab-indented mail would slip through the obligations filter and could open an obligation from agent mail. That's a real drift bug, though low probability. Since the comment claims "mirrors isSyntheticUserText locally", the mirror is already inaccurate at birth. That's worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Given "a misclassifying judge must never invent obligations" is the PR's own precision-first principle, and agent mail is exactly the kind of content that must never open obligations (mail is data), I'd rate this IMPORTANT... ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: windowed rehydration can silently erase the ledger (data loss) — the #488 failure mode this slice re-creates**

`latestObligationsLedgerIn` reads `Session.getEntries()`, but the CLI's default resume path opens sessions **windowed** (`session_commands.dart:572`, `_repo.open(metadata, windowed: true)`), and `WindowedSessionStorage.getEntries()` returns only the resident tail (paged back just to the newest compaction boundary / parity token budget). For any marathon session — exactly the sessions where obligations accumulate — the latest `obligations_ledger` snapshot routinely lies below the resident tail. Two consequences:

1. **Projection silently loses the block** — `_withObligationsBlock` (session_tree.dart) sees no ledger record and renders nothing, breaking the slice's own HARD invariant ("compaction can never sink an obligation") in the only wired host.
2. **Worse — permanent data loss.** `_obligationsWriterFor` (agent_cli_persist.dart:85-93) rehydrates the writer from the same truncated view. The next classified message then appends a snapshot that **wholesale-replaces** the ledger (latest-snapshot-wins), permanently dropping every entry recorded before the boundary. The file's older snapshots survive as audit, but the effective ledger is erased.

The sibling registry hit this exact failure and it was not hypothetical — `agent_cli.dart:454-457`: "the windowed boot open drops side-leaf custom records out of getEntries — the registry used to come back EMPTY on every restart" (issue #488), fixed by a raw file scan. The scan API already exists: `repo.readCustomRecordsOfType(parent, {obligationsLedgerRecordType})` (see `subagentRegistryRows` in `lib/src/task/child_session_io.dart`). The PR defers this as "mechanical upgrade if a regression ever shows a missed snapshot", but the regression already showed for the sibling, and here the blast radius is larger than a missed render — it is silent ledger erasure on the default resume path.

**Fix in this slice**: rehydrate the writer (and the projection's `latestObligationsLedgerIn` lookup, or at least the writer) from the raw scan — `readCustomRecordsOfType` — instead of `getEntries()`. Add a regression test that opens the session windowed after the snapshot slides out of residency.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: engine gate ignores the live settings override (`liveCompactionEngine`)**

`_ingestObligations` gates on `config.compactionEngine ?? CompactionEngine.structured`, but the established resolution chain everywhere else includes the live override (issue #288):

```dart
// agent_cli_compaction.dart:470-472 — the pattern to match
engine: config.liveCompactionEngine ??
    config.compactionEngine ??
    CompactionEngine.structured,
// also agent_cli.dart:484-485 (subagent children)
```

Divergence when a user flips the engine in the live settings flow:

- `compaction.engine: classic` in config + live override `structured` → the session compacts structured but **never classifies** (E3 gate wrongly trips) — obligations are silently missing.
- config null/structured + live override `classic` → classification keeps firing while the session runs classic. Harmless-ish, but the gate no longer describes the session's engine.

One-line fix: resolve through `config.liveCompactionEngine ?? config.compactionEngine ?? CompactionEngine.structured` (or extract the resolution into a helper both call sites share).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
